llm.summary: The skill's files, instructions, and environment requirement (SEAART_TOKEN) are consistent with its stated purpose of driving SeaArt video generation; there are a few minor operational/documentation gaps to be aware of but no signs of misdirection or excessive privileges.

dimensions.detail: The skill is explicitly a SeaArt video generator and only requests a SeaArt auth token (T) and uses Python to call SeaArt APIs — this is coherent. Minor inconsistencies: the SKILL.md metadata lists python3 as a required binary while the registry metadata showed none; the code relies on the 'requests' library but there is no install step to ensure that dependency is present.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions focus on obtaining the SeaArt cookie, setting SEAART_TOKEN, and running the included Python script which only posts prompts/image URLs to seaart.ai and polls for results. The skill does instruct the agent/operator to echo $SEAART_TOKEN (to check presence) and to persist the token via /update-config — these are reasonable but worth caution (see user guidance). The instructions do not ask for unrelated files, credentials, or endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only install), which reduces supply-chain risk. However, the repository includes a Python script that assumes a particular skill path (~/.claude/skills/seaart-video/...) and requires the 'requests' package; no automated install or dependency enforcement is provided. This is an operational gap rather than a sign of malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only required environment variable is SEAART_TOKEN, which is appropriate. The skill persists the token into the agent config using /update-config (as documented) — persisting an auth cookie locally is expected but increases the importance of protecting that config file (permission and access control).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' or any elevated/system-wide privileges. It does persist the token to the local agent config per its instructions, but it does not modify other skills or global system settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it sends your prompt and any image URLs (and the SEAART token cookie) to seaart.ai to create videos. Before installing or running it: (1) review scripts/generate.py yourself to confirm behavior; (2) ensure Python 3 and the 'requests' package are installed (pip install requests), since no install step is provided; (3) avoid pasting the token into chat — follow the described cookie-extraction and use /update-config to set SEAART_TOKEN if you accept persisting the token locally; (4) tighten permissions on the agent config (e.g., chmod 600) because the token is stored there; (5) consider creating a SeaArt account or token dedicated to this use so you can revoke it if needed; and (6) if you expect this to run on a different environment than the assumed ~/.claude/skills/... path, adjust the command or file placement accordingly.
